narrative:
The model estimated your chance of being a bad credit risk at 26.0%. That does not mean default is certain; it means the estimated risk was above the lender’s cut-off for this loan, so the application was denied.

The most influential factor was having a guarantor, and it worked in your favour by reducing the estimated risk. The second most important factor was the requested 12-month term, which is shorter than the 19.17-month average among approved applicants and also reduced risk. The third most important factor was your checking account being below zero DM. That pushed toward bad credit and was the main adverse signal among the top factors; only about 12.6% of approved applicants had an overdrawn account like yours. So although the guarantor and short term helped, the remaining risk, led by the overdrawn checking account, stayed above the lender’s limit.

Next, focus on bringing your checking account into a positive balance and keeping it there for several months before reapplying. Ask the lender which account conduct or risk cut-off you need to meet, and whether keeping the guarantor or requesting a shorter or smaller loan would help. Reapplying after your account history improves is more likely to produce a different decision.
